focus: Q3 repair audit: compare every setup-battery repair and the hooks, standards, and setup targets with the operation they actually perform
noveltyJustification: Six findings isolate repair-path defects not established by the prior false-healthy and documentation passes; two partly overlap those earlier topics.
keyQuestions: Q3: Which repairs named by the battery or by /doctor:git targets are wrong, incomplete or unsafe for the failure they claim to fix?
answeredQuestions: Q3: Which repairs named by the battery or by /doctor:git targets are wrong, incomplete or unsafe for the failure they claim to fix?
ruledOut: The AI-tool registration repair pointer was not ranked as incorrect: its linked README section gives per-runtime event and wiring details.

label: The install repair is not reliably corrective: the suggested bare /doctor:update runs the update check, which is read-only, while the git restore example targets the whole sk-git skill directory even when only one required path is missing. Replace it with an exact missing-file recovery path or an explicit reviewed update/apply route.

When the inspected repository carries the toolchain sentinel, the hook repair tells the operator to execute that repository's own install-git-hooks.sh. This crosses the battery's own trust boundary and installs repository-supplied hooks; the repair should require trust review or point to a verified installer source.

The gates repair is self-referential for helper/report failures: /doctor:git hooks starts by running the same git-hook-gates.cjs list command that failed in setup. Separately, saved-off gates are returned as PASS details, so the battery emits no repair for the state that hooks can actually change.

The standards repair cannot recover a missing configured contract directory: setup reports /doctor:git standards, but every git-standards mode resolves skgit.contractDir first and aborts when it points to a missing directory; the interactive workflow begins with status and cannot reach init.

The worktree repair always changes git config, but SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE takes precedence over that config. When the failing base came from the environment, the printed config command does not change the value the check just reported.

The Commit-Id repair offers skilled.commitId=false as an equal alternative to restoring a missing allocator. The policy helper gives that local false value precedence over repository markers, so this makes the check pass by disabling Commit-Id enforcement rather than repairing the missing allocator; label it explicitly as an opt-out.

The advisory-rules repair always says to fix a check name, but the same repair is used for invalid JSON and a non-array root as well as unknown or missing check names. Emit cause-specific guidance so syntax and shape failures do not receive the wrong repair.

The suppression repair only says unset the reported master-switch variables. That works when they are set in the operator's current shell, but it will not change a value injected by an IDE or agent host into the checker process; show the variable source and tell the operator to update that launch environment and restart when applicable.
